title: Diagnosing async performance problems
description: Use ETW, EventCounters, and profiling tools to find async bottlenecks and thread pool issues.

data.text: Production async problems are rarely obvious from code alone. Thread pool starvation, excessive allocations, and lock contention show up as latency spikes or throughput drops. The right tools let you pinpoint the cause without guessing.

items: **dotnet-trace** — Lightweight ETW-based profiler for .NET 6+. Collects CPU samples, thread pool events, and async method timelines.
**PerfView** — Rich ETW viewer that can analyze thread pool starvation, GC pressure, and async method duration.
**EventCounters** — Real-time metrics from the runtime, including `threadpool.queue.length` and `threadpool.thread.count`.

data.title: Collecting a trace with dotnet-trace
data.code:
dotnet-trace collect --process-id <PID> \
  --providers Microsoft-DotNETCore-EventPipe \
  --duration 00:01:00 \
  trace.nettrace

# View thread pool queue length in real time
# Look for threadpool.queue.length and threadpool.thread.count events

rows: PerfView CPU samples stuck in Monitor.Enter
Thread stacks showing blocked on Task.Wait()

data.title: EventCounters for live monitoring
data.code:
dotnet-counters monitor --process-id <PID> \
  System.Threading.ThreadPool \
  System.Runtime \
  Microsoft-AspNetCore-Server-Kestrel

# Watch:
#   threadpool.queue.length
#   threadpool.thread.count
#   gc-heap-size
#   requests-per-second

data.title: Monitor in production, not just dev
data.text: Performance problems often appear only under real load. Enable EventCounters in staging and production so you can correlate latency spikes with thread pool metrics before customers notice.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Use PerfView for deep analysis of thread pool and GC behavior.
Correlate latency spikes with thread pool queue length and CPU samples.
EventCounters give real-time visibility into runtime health.
